cards.a_html:
1. It is an approach that analyzes audit risks, sets materiality thresholds based on audit risk analysis & develops audit programmes that allocate large portion of audit resources to high risk areas.
2. Auditor doesn’t need to perform audit procedures on all areas of audit.
3. 3 key steps – o Assessing ROMM in FS o Designing and performing further audit procedures that respond to assessed risks & reduce ROMM to acceptably low level o Issuing appropriate audit report based on audit findings

cards.q: Audit risk components
cards.q_html: <mark class="kw">Audit risk</mark> components
cards.a_html:
• Inherent Risk -
  • Susceptibility of assertion to misstatement that could be material, assuming that there

are no controls.

  • It arises from entity's size, objectives, operations, complexity & regulatory environment.
  • Eg, technological development making product obsolete.
  • Control Risk -
  • Risk that internal control system will not prevent/detect/correct material misstatement
  • Internal control is missing.
  • Some control risk always exists because of inherent limitations of internal control.
  • Detection Risk -
  • Risk that auditor will not detect material misstatement even if all audit procedures applied.
  • It has inverse relation to ROMM at assertion level.

Audit Risk - Risk that auditor will issue inappropriate opinion while FS are materially misstated.

AUDIT RISK = ROMM x Detection Risk

ROMM = Inherent Risk x Control Risk

  • ROMM = Risk that material misstatement may exist in FS before start of audit.
  • Audit materiality has inverse relation with audit risk.

cards.q: Table — SA 450 – Evaluation of Misstatements Identified (p.46)
cards.q_html: Table — SA 450 – Evaluation of Misstatements Identified (p.46)
cards.a_html:
• SA 450 – Evaluation of Misstatements Identified During the Audit Q1) Definitions Misstatement Difference between amount, classification, presentation, disclosure of FS item & amount, classification, presentation, disclosure required as per applicable financial reporting framework. Misstatements can arise from error/ fraud. Uncorrected Misstatements Misstatements that auditor has accumulated during audit & that have not been corrected. Factual misstatements Misstatements about which there is no doubt. Judgmental misstatements Differences arising from judgements of mgt concerning accounting estimates that auditor considers unreasonable or selection or application of accounting policies that auditor considers inappropriate. Projected misstatements Auditor’s best estimate of misstatements in populations, involving projection of misstatements identified in audit samples to entire populations from which samples were drawn. Q2) Accumulation of identified Misstatements 1. Auditor shall accumulate misstatements identified during audit, other than those that are clearly trivial. 2. Accumulation of clearly trivial amounts would not have a material effect on FS. 3. When there is uncertainty about whether item is clearly trivial, it is considered not to be clearly trivial. Q3) Consideration of identified misstatements as audit progresses Auditor shall determine whether overall audit strategy & audit plan need to be revised, if – Nature of identified misstatements & Aggregate of misstatements accumulated during circumstances of their occurrence indicate that audit approaches materiality determined as per other misstatements may exist that, when SA 320 aggregated with misstatements accumulated during the audit, could be material If, at auditor’s request, mgt has examined class of transactions, account balance, disclosure & corrected misstatements that were detected, auditor shall perform additional audit procedures to determine whether misstatements remain. Q4) Communication & Correction of Misstatements 1. Auditor shall communicate all misstatements accumulated during audit with mgt, unless prohibited by Law or regulation. 2. Auditor shall request mgt to correct misstatements 3. If mgt refuses to correct misstatements communicated by auditor, auditor shall obtain understanding of mgt’s reasons for not making corrections & shall take that understanding into account when evaluating whether FS as a whole are free of material misstatements

cards.q: Basic points
cards.q_html: Basic points
cards.a_html:
1. Going concern is a fundamental accounting assumption
  2. If company is a going concern, FS are prepared on assumption that it will continue its

  3. Preliminary assessment of going concern is performed by management.

cards.a_html:
SA 610 – Using the Work of Internal Auditor Q1) Basics 1. External auditor has sole responsibility of audit opinion & is not reduced by use of internal auditor’s work. 2. External auditor should be independent. But there is no such requirement for internal auditor. 3. Using work of internal auditor can be categorised into 2 types - Using work of Internal Audit Function Using internal auditors to provide direct assistance under direction, supervision, review of external auditors 4. Summary FS (SFS) are less detailed but provides structured representation consistent with FS.
